theorem.name: R5_E8_PAYLOAD_BACKBONE_RIGIDITY_V1

payload_restriction_branch_stability.claim: Fixing one payload z does not erase any already-projected odd-selector assignment coordinate from the frozen structural branch signatures.
proof: For every projected odd selector x_i, its branch-local residual is A_i or B_i, both two-literal payload clauses.
A fixed payload z occurs in at most one of A_i and B_i for a given block.
Restricting z in the residual that contains it yields either TRUE or the other literal, never FALSE; the alternative residual remains a nonconstant two-literal clause.

The residual is paired in the frozen block tree with the unresolved even block G_{i+1} (for odd i), which remains nonconstant after any single payload restriction because z occurs in at most one of its two selector clauses; the other clause still contains the unresolved even selector.
Therefore the two local odd-assignment alternatives remain structurally distinct and noncomplementary after z=0 or z=1.

Induction through the complete block tree and through previously introduced Shannon-OR nodes preserves assignment-signature injectivity: distinct partial odd assignments retain distinct child-ref pairs and cannot trigger IDEMPOTENCE or COMPLEMENT.
Any old z-independent local node bypassed when a z-literal satisfies its clause is exposed by the opposite cofactor where that literal is unsatisfied.
Unaffected clause and sibling-subtree refs remain reachable.
Projected-odd residual nodes not containing z remain unchanged.

Above the local support, payload-restriction branch stability prevents a dependent ancestor from collapsing both cofactor paths; z-independent siblings therefore remain reachable in at least one rebuilt path.
Hence every old z-independent reachable node appears in at least one of the two cofactors and therefore in Q_z.

z is second payload literal after selector

projected_odd_blocks: If an odd support block has already been projected, its original selector block has been replaced on branches by A_i or B_i.
z appears in at most one of those residuals.
A z-dependent residual is one two-literal OR node; across z=0/1 it can contribute at most two local savings.
Thus projecting an odd support selector cannot increase the original local savings budget assigned to that occurrence block.
backbone: Every z-dependent node above the four local occurrence neighborhoods rebuilds to a distinct reachable structural node in each cofactor because assignment signatures remain distinct.
Therefore the Shannon/block-tree backbone contributes no additional savings beyond the local budget.
